transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-11 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 1h15m | Recorded by: Fireflies
Attendees: Elena Park, Miguel Alvarez, Priya Singh, Jordan Lee, Avery Chen, Katerina Rossi, Samir Patel, Nora Davis (obs)

=== Summary (auto) ===
Elena: okay so main goal here is to make sure the Q1 launch readiness checklist is complete and owners are clear. we want no surprises in january.

=== Transcript ===
[00:00] Elena (PM): alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — agenda is checkpoints, launch gates, perf and incident readiness, and docs. if anything missing shout out.
[00:18] Miguel (Eng Manager): sounds good, elena. i'll start with infra perf — we've got the first pass of benchmarks but there is some noise on the dedicated pools for long tail latency when sequence length spikes.
[00:32] Priya (Staff SWE): mhm, i've seen that too in the nightly runs, especially on 8k sequences, the kv cache eviction pattern is causing stutters.
[00:47] Jordan (SRE): yeah and to add, the autoscaler sometimes overshoots on burst because of request clustering from our canary traffic generator, so that makes cost estimates fuzzy.
[01:05] Elena: okay that's important for the cost SLO. Katerina, from product perspective — what's the hard launch date window we're targeting?
[01:18] Katerina (VP Product): we want the public launch early january, ideally first two weeks, but everything needs to be signed off by 2027-01-03 for marketing readiness. so internal handoffs need to be complete by end of this year.
[01:34] Samir (CTO): noted. that gives us a couple of weeks to finalize canary rules and perform a smoke benchmark. Miguel, is that feasible?
[01:45] Miguel: yeah feasible, we need to re-run benchmarks with controlled prefix caching enabled and a longer tail run to surface those 95/99 spikes. estimate two runs ~24 hours each.
[02:02] Priya: also can we validate quantization profiles across our most common model variants? some of the regression we saw might be quant-related.
[02:13] Miguel: yes, i'll include q4 quant profiles in the benchmark matrix.
[02:20] Jordan: for canary criteria, can we agree to start with a small percent, 2% traffic for 48 hours, and have automatic rollback if latency p99 increases by >20% or error-rate >0.1%?
[02:36] Elena: that sounds reasonable, though product might want stricter error tolerances. Katerina?
[02:40] Katerina: let's keep the error-rate threshold at 0.05% for the first canary cohort, then loosen for broader rollout. we need low false-positive for customer impact.
[02:52] Avery (Product Ops): i'll document the two-stage canary: stage 1 (2% x48h) error-rate 0.05% p99 delta 15%; stage 2 (10% x24h) error-rate 0.1% p99 delta 20%.
[03:08] Elena: good, that gives engineering strict rollback gates.
[03:12] Miguel: small note — for private deployments, the customer-managed KMS and network egress adds variability; we should have a checklist item to validate KMS integration in the on-prem staging env.
[03:26] Priya: agreed. i've seen a mismatch where key rotation intervals caused a brief auth hiccup in one test cluster.
[03:33] Jordan: also need to confirm RBAC for the private control plane and that audit log retention meets compliance. Nora, can legal sign off on retention defaults?
[03:44] Nora (Legal): we'll need a short review, but the proposed defaults (90 days for shared, 365 for enterprise) look fine pending customer opt-in. i'll add it as an item.
[03:58] Elena: thanks. on incident playbooks — Priya, Jordan, who takes top-3 P0s?
[04:05] Priya: i'll own KV cache corruption and model mismatch issues. Jordan will own routing/plateau scaling incidents and infra failures.
[04:14] Jordan: yep, and i'll also update on-call rotation doc to include a staging pager for launch week.
[04:21] Avery: for GTM dry-run, we should include a scenario for a canary rollback and communications flow to customers and sales. i'll set that up.
[04:33] Elena: perfect. next — docs and runbooks, where will they live?
[04:38] Miguel: we'll centralize in the internal docs repo, under /launches/q1-2027. i'll create pointers from the runbook to the playbooks and perf spreadsheets.
[04:48] Priya: can we also create a condensed one-page ops checklist for the on-call and SREs? short action list to follow during incidents.
[04:58] Jordan: yes, single-page TL;DR is helpful. i'll draft.
[05:03] Katerina: one more ask from product — need a mapping of features to risk level and required validation tests. that helps prioritize the test matrix.
[05:15] Elena: ok, we'll add that to the checklist.
[05:18] Miguel: regarding benchmarks, i'll need access to the dedicated pools for a controlled run; Avery, can you coordinate capacity reservations?
[05:27] Avery: yes i'll coordinate with infra ops. i'll also flag quota for the private staging env.
[05:34] Elena: thanks. anything else on dependencies?
[05:37] Priya: security review — we still need the SOC2 evidence packet for the private deployment templates. Nora, can legal/security provide an ETA?
[05:47] Nora: security is compiling the packet this week, we can have a draft by 2026-12-16, final by 2026-12-22 depending on vendor responses.
[05:56] Samir: we should run an end-to-end failover test before we open canary traffic; that needs a rehearsal window. recommend a dry-run on 2026-12-20 as Avery suggested.
[06:08] Elena: ok, tag that as required.
[06:10] Miguel: small slip — the nightly image bake currently includes a kernel patch that increased inference stability but changed the container start time; i want to validate startup latency doesn't affect cold start SLO.
[06:25] Priya: good catch, i'll add cold-start latency to the benchmark targets.
[06:30] Katerina: how are we handling pricing comms? we need final unit economics before marketing copy.
[06:37] Avery: finance is finalizing the numbers, but we need per-token cost and expected average token length. Miguel, can you provide estimated per-token infra cost from the benchmark?
[06:46] Miguel: yes after the controlled runs i'll produce per-token and tail-cost estimates.
[06:50] Elena: wrap up — recap owners and dates.
[06:54] Elena: Elena to publish checklist by 2026-12-13; Miguel perf by 2026-12-17; Priya/Jordan incident playbooks by 2026-12-16; Avery GTM dry-run 2026-12-20. Nora security packet draft by 2026-12-16. Any objections?
[07:10] Samir: no objections.
[07:12] Nora: none.
[07:14] Katerina: looks good.
[07:18] Elena: ok thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the doc links. Link to draft checklist: https://internal.redwood.com/launches/q1-2027/checklist (internal)
[07:30] Miguel: one last note — we should schedule the runtime deep-dive for benchmarks with SE/runtime team next week; i'll propose times.
[07:38] Elena: noted. thanks all. meeting adjourned.
